assumptions: The time window is 22 October to 31 October 2026, as explicitly requested.
A risk decline means any failure with category risk_decline, which includes ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE, RISK_RULE_DECLINE and SUSPECTED_FRAUD.
caveats: Attempt volume from 22 to 31 October was 39% above the usual level for those weekdays. This can come from real business events such as sales, or from data gaps, so check before comparing totals across this period. It is not treated as a data error by itself.
The ranking shows counts of risk-declined attempts, not decline rates, so high-volume BINs may rank higher simply because they have more traffic.

facts.text: There were 2,516 failed card attempts with a risk-decline reason between 2026-10-22 and 2026-10-31.
BIN 911001 (Harbor Bank) had the most risk declines: 371 failed attempts, 14.8% of the total.
BIN 911003 (Harbor Bank) was second with 345 failed attempts (13.7% of the total), and BIN 911002 (Harbor Bank) was third with 297 (11.8%).
The top three BINs together account for 40.3% of all risk declines in the period.
After the top three, the next BINs are far smaller: 922002 (Lotus Bank) with 92 failed attempts (3.7%), 922003 (Lotus Bank) with 91 (3.6%), and 912002 (Harbor Bank) with 76 (3.0%).
Harbor Bank appears four times in the top 10 BINs (911001, 911003, 911002, 912002), more than any other issuer.
Attempt volume in this period was 39% higher than the usual level for those weekdays.

response.headline: Three Harbor Bank BINs (911001, 911003 and 911002) had the most risk declines from 22 to 31 October 2026, together accounting for 40.3% of the 2,516 risk-decline failed attempts on card payments.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Compare risk-decline rates (declines per attempt) for these BINs against other issuers over a normal period, and check the split between ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE, RISK_RULE_DECLINE and SUSPECTED_FRAUD for these BINs.
hypotheses.rationale: Three Harbor Bank BINs sit far above every other BIN (297 to 371 failed attempts versus 92 or fewer), but the evidence shows only counts, not the reason behind them.
hypotheses.text: Harbor Bank's risk rules may be stricter than other issuers' for these BINs, which would explain why their declines are concentrated in three BINs.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Calculate risk-decline rate per BIN for these 10 days and for a prior comparable 10-day window.
hypotheses.rationale: Attempt volume was 39% above usual, and raw counts naturally rise with volume. The evidence ranks counts, not rates.
hypotheses.text: The volume spike in this period may have inflated risk-decline counts for the highest-volume BINs without any change in their decline rate.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: Facts on BINs 911001, 911003 and 911002; hypothesis on volume spike inflating counts
recommendations.rationale: Counts alone cannot show whether these BINs are declining at an unusually high rate or are just high-volume.
recommendations.text: Review risk-decline rates (not just counts) for BINs 911001, 911003 and 911002 against their total attempt volumes.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: Hypothesis on Harbor Bank's stricter risk rules
recommendations.rationale: Harbor Bank accounts for four of the top 10 BINs, including the top three.
recommendations.text: Engage Harbor Bank to understand their risk rules and whether any are blocking legitimate transactions on these BINs.
